sentences.text: Back to my desk to grab a pen.
No worries.
Good to see everybody.
How you doing, Chris?
Good.
Good morning.
Morning.
Nice to see you.
Hello, can you hear me?
Who have we got?
Hey, Kathy, how you doing?
I'm doing great.
How are you?
Yeah, really good, thank you.
All right, almost there.
We got Michael, how you doing?
And somebody else for your team.
I'm good.
I'm bringing back the.
Turtleneck.
I just wanted to let you know in advance.
I think it must be a thing we're wearing the same outfit.
Maybe.
Well, you have a nice.
Yours is a little thicker.
You have a nice blazer.
You know, I put the blazer on, I just look.
I literally look like a turtle.
I look like a fisherman if I don't put the blazer on too.
You look like a fisherman and I look like a turtle.
This is true.
Perfect.
Well, good to see everybody.
Obviously our role is, is just to accommodate the meeting of mind, but I think if we could just introduce ourselves, maybe Michael, and a few words with.
About your company and what you do.
And then Kathy.
The same.
And then we can go into some, some questions about the business and what you're interested in, Michael.
Sure.
I should kick off.
Yeah.
And just to let you know, everybody, that we're recording today's session as well.
So if anybody needs the recording later, they can get it.
Well, great.
Hi, I'm Michael Basak.
I founded Axle about 14 years ago and ever since then we've been investing in incubating, acquiring businesses in the sort.
Of tech enabled marketing services space.
Primarily media focused businesses.
Throughout that journey.
Sometimes I get sucked in and wind up running media businesses.
So I don't know if you're familiar.
With an agency called assembly, which is.
Part of the Stagwell Network, about 1,500.
Employees and I was the CEO of that business.
Prior to that, I served on the.
Board there for six years.
So my career has squarely been in media.
Not yet announced, but we just closed on the sale of three media businesses in the past few weeks, two of which I founded or co founded and.
One of which we acquired in 2022.
And this is pretty much the first time in 14 years where we have in a sense exited all the businesses.
That we either incubated or acquired.
And we are in this very unique.
Space right now where we get to sort of take a look at the landscape more broadly and say, where do we want to go next?
So we've been spending a lot of.
Time looking in the CTV space on the SSP side, on the dsp Side.
On the, I'd say like specialist CTV.
Focused performance, focused media agency side.
So obviously when I saw Andy's email, you know, I never know whether it's.
His email or whether his name is just on the, on the to line.
But the email that purportedly came from.
Andy, it just instantly sort of said, this is a business that I'm curious about.
I have admittedly absolutely zero experience.
I'll caveat it, of course, in traditional media, except to say I know how incredibly complex it is, especially in the local level, and I know that a.
Lot of people have tried to solve.
This and at the same time I.
Know there's just a tremendous amount of.
Change in traditional media.
So I guess the third caveat would.
Be it still seems to be incredibly.
Important, incredibly valuable.
And perhaps as viewership.
Continues to decrease in linear, maybe that's even just more of an opportunity to be offering expertise to reach that audience.
Because I'm sure, as you know, there is a lot of unduplicated reach, especially among older audiences.
So I don't, certainly wouldn't say it's going away anytime soon, but certainly becoming.
More challenging to grow those businesses that focus.
And that was why I like that you guys have already sort of made that pivot.
And then the last is, I think like two or three years ago I was like fairly confident that like, yeah, we'll just keep on doing what we've been doing.
We'll find like great founders and great management teams who built great businesses in.
The marketing space and we'll just like continue to grow those businesses and partner with those entrepreneurs and those leaders.
And I think the last two years.
Have shown that we probably are in.
A significant period of change.
And AI is absolutely going to disrupt.
Every aspect of media planning and buying.
And in speaking with brands and speaking.

With other agencies, like if you're not already have hired technologists internally to be building this type of software or working with outside contractors who specialize in helping agencies, then you're already like a little behind.
But not all hope is lost.
But it's just a really interesting time to be in this space.
So I'm excited.
It was a very long intro, it was a good like five minutes, but hopefully gave you a sense, I'll say that the companies that they're on the.
Website, so it's not like there's a mystery.
The companies that just transacted are one.
Of the largest political digital media businesses.
A company called DS Political and a company called Effective Spend that we had.
Also rebranded as optimal, which is A lower funnel performance marketing agency, so search and social, but certainly moving into ctv.
And then the third business is a.
Healthcare data business that primarily licenses audience.
Just like in the Liveramp and other data stores, and then also creates PMPs.
But specifically focused on privacy around patient data.
So those are some of the areas.
That have been focused on lately.
Yay.
Hey, thanks for that, Michael.
So Kathy and Chris, how about just a quick intro for yourselves what you both do, job titles and then we can get into some questions and backwards and forwards.
Okay, I'll start.
I apologize for the black screen.
I didn't wear my turtleneck today, so I felt like I needed to hide my face.
Actually, I'm having some technical difficulties here in the boonies, But I started CTV 46 years ago in the basement of my house.
And the business started off as local cable.
Within two years it expanded into regional, including broadcast.
Within five years we were doing everything video, everything linear from very high end advertisers doing national business.
We started with Sony Classics, was one of our major clients that came on board, spent about 20 million with us, allowed us to expand the business, get a move into a very nice office space.
About five years after that we actually purchased a building in Powell, Ohio.
And we house 25 employees in this building currently.
But I think the main benefit of our company is that it has the ability to grow quickly.
We are working with four in house salespeople, two outsized sales people, mainly because it was a comfortable number for me.
I made a good living.
I was not that motivated to blooming into what it could be, which is a very much bigger organization.
So this opportunity to have someone come in with resources, have someone like Chris who is motivated to grow the business is an exceptional opportunity.
Also in the way of CTV, we have grown that business year over year, 52%.
We are hoping to continue that those efforts throughout 2026 and 2027.
We have a strong AI partner in an outside company.
It's a digital company with whom we've done several millions of dollars worth of business.
They are top shelf.
We actually vetted it, vetted three very large companies out York and they were the the top performer.
So in a nutshell, that's what CTV is all about.
Chris, as of Monday became CEO of ctv.
I remain president.
Congratulations.
I would like to introduce Chris at this point.
Hi, it's nice to meet you.
I am fortunate to work with this incredible team of people every day.
And you're right, we do have a very strong traditional background.
It is complicated, it is often labor Intensive.
However, we're a very lean company and I feel like we've done quite a good job of making it as efficient as possible, both as far as manpower and cost, which is important with traditional.
But we've also really obviously leaned into ctv, I'm going to say streaming.
Since our name is ctv, it can kind of become a little confusing.
And those two just like you said, really complement each other.
And we have invested in in technology and streaming partners that allow us to report to our clients that minimal overlap between those two audiences.
Kathy had mentioned we have multiple streaming DSP partners that we work with, be it performance driven.
As you had mentioned, we do cost per sale campaigns for clients as well as CPA campaigns.

Our digital CPM, our streaming CPMs are quite competitive and because we do a lot of business with the national networks, our private Marketplace MPG Deal CPMs are favorable and more affordable than people that are sitting on the trade desk transacting.
So that's been beneficial to us.

One of the things that I've really realized in the past couple of months, especially you know, some agencies that we work with, that they have a seat on the trade desk and they do their own streaming, but there's certain content they don't have access to unless they buy directly with the national network.

And I'm currently working on several million dollars in streaming only campaigns that have to be bought directly with that network group because they're not going to get an appear and get sponsorships and billboards within this streaming only content if they buy it on the trade desk.
So there's a lot of possibility for us to leverage those traditional relationships and make it even more beneficial in the streaming digital space as well.
And so I really see that as a benefit going forward as well as yes, like linear viewing is shrinking and it is tend to shift a bit more towards streaming.

But there's still a ton of stream sports content that is linear and if you really want those eyeballs, they're on linear television, you know, buying the local broadcast station or buying NBC nationally and there's a lot of opportunity there and those digital companies don't know how to do it.
We have the ratings, the resources, the contacts and we're so fortunate.

Like you know, we have contacts that we've worked with for well over 20 years and they work really hard for us because we're not just like some big holding company, we're bringing first time advertisers, we're growing business that people are really excited about.
And so we're really fortunate in that case, another big benefit is because we do national, we do local, we do direct response television as well.
We really look at these RFPs through a different lens than some of your traditional media agencies.
So I have an agency that came to us and wanted to do just some local television, but they wanted to reach some C suite people, which meant they wanted cable news networks.
And because of subscription fragmentation, I really diverted them away from buying the cable in local markets and let's buy it nationally directly with those cable networks.
It's pretty affordable and would give them a lot more visibility.

So there's a lot of things like that that are beneficial as well, as we're using best in class technology to help support our recommendations and research where these audiences are, as well as our own dashboard that helps us go from RFP to invoice in flight clearance as well that we own.
So it's not domo or tableau where you've got like all those license.
We had, like, we have enough licensing fees with Nielsen and stuff like that.
We own this and we can continue to evolve it and make it more of, of what we want and need, like, over time.
So I'm just going to pause there.
I've kind of given you a lot and would love to, you know, address any questions.
It's really nice meeting you both.
Congratulations again on your recent promotion.
Oh, thank you.
Yeah, it's very exciting.
I have, I've so far written down 12 questions and I am also mindful that we have 12 minutes.
Not that I have a major hard stop, but I think I could basically riff on all 12 of my questions.
To just show you some of the.
Kind of questions I have.
And then either we can maybe cherry.
Pick one or two of them that we feel like talking about now.

And then I could follow up and obviously Ahmed and Andy can tell me whether or not I will be invited, if it exists yet, to sort of further conversations, analyze some of the data on the business historically.
The one thing I'll just start with is that I might have a client for you guys that I'll talk to the cmo.
So Fairview Health, it's like the second largest hospital system in Minnesota, and they're about to do a whole rebrand and relaunch of, of Fairview.
And so they hired Optimal to do.
All their performance marketing.
But now they.
I spoke with the CMO yesterday who asked me, you know, hey, you guys.
Don'T do linear and traditional.
If we're going to do a lot of like, local.
And he mentioned radio and out of home.
So I didn't know.
In addition to obviously streaming and video, do you also plan all other sort of local channels as well, like radio and out of home as well?
So I could just start with there and then if so I'll send an.
Email to Chris and just say, hey.
Who'S the name of the.
Sorry, also the name of a CMO of Fairview and I'll connect you guys as well.
But I just sort of curious like what other channels or not.
Which is cool too.
Yeah, we've done radio.
That's terrestrial radio.
That's an option out of home really isn't our wheelhouse.
Although there is out of home you can access digitally.
You know what I mean?
But that really, I mean you really need to partner with somebody.
If they were, if they were doing television and wanted television, then we could, I would say we can absolutely partner with another expert to fill in the gap for the out of home.
But if they're only looking at radio and out of home, I'm not necessarily sure we're the perfect fit.
Only if they were also going to do television.
Does that make sense?
Okay, it does.
I'll find out.
Okay, great.
Okay, here we go.
Lots of questions.
I'm going to ramble at all my questions.
So just to give you a sense.
Of what I'm looking at, if that makes sense.
So first you mentioned, and this isn't.
In any order, you know, the DSPs that you license.
I'm sort of curious which, I'll go through all the questions, which DSPs you're licensing currently.
And you said you're accessing unique supply from some relationships you have.
Sort of curious, like to talk a little bit about understanding those unique supply relationships.
And then are you and your employees doing the trading within those DSPs or.
Are you sort of asking those DSPS to help with Mapster?
Okay, great.
And then wait, we already answered a question you mentioned.
I think Kathy mentioned having spent millions of dollars with an AI company.
I didn't know what the context was.
Are they a client of yours or.
To help you all build?
So curious about what that was all.
About because that sounded exciting.
Especially I'm in New York, so I'm like, oh, go visit them.
I'm curious about the business.
When I looked at the SIP itself, there was so much tech in there and so much data.
And I'm very curious and maybe we could schedule a longer conversation to really actually walk through the presentation very slowly, like as a management presentation, because it.
Was so fascinating to me to see.
Some of the tech that you mentioned like was proprietary and some of it obviously I'm sure is licensed.
And just sort of curious in terms.
Of all the technology and how, how.
It dovetails with, with the AI that, that you're investing in as well.
I'm curious along those lines, I think would be the first set of questions.
And then we could talk a little bit more about the business itself, how you price.
It's obvious it's a pretty low margin business right now and sort of where you see opportunity to increase margins, whether.
It'S through data that you provide that we can curate and create our own.
Audience segments which could have margin, whether it's non transparent media buying, but doing so transparently.
Is everything you do transparent?
Are all your commissions transparent?
Because I think that's a struggle that.
A lot of that's why the larger.
Holding companies are doing well is because they figured out ways to extract additional margin in media.
And obviously those who are just charging at a transparent margin are losing money.
Unable to weather storms, dependent on whale clients.
I'm curious, are we like, nope, we have to be transparent.
Doesn't matter.
I don't care if it's profitable or not or are we open to, hey, we want to run a business, we want to grow, we want to invest in all these areas.
But looking at the P and L for the last few years and the.
Dependence on the whale client sort of.
Makes me think like we should be trying to figure out some higher margin.
Ways to grow the business.
So curious about your thoughts on that.
And then I'll just add in the end like where do you want to go?
What are you looking for in a partner?
What's the future look like?
What excites you about this sort of next chapter?
But those were like the whole host of questions.
I just sort of figured with six minutes left rather that it's more fun to have a conversation.
So I'll just sort of like leave it all there and we can just chat.
I wanted to address the DSPs that we work with.
We don't license, we don't pay a licensing fee.
They want our business so they just open their doors to us.
And the partner that we have, our strongest partner, has developed a really strong AI platform.
And that's where we find tremendous opportunity to grow the streaming part of our business as far as tech.
CTV owns a proprietary database called Cable Base.
It's trademarked, it has every single cable system in the country's rates by network, by day part, it's automated.
So our sort of claim to fame in the cable world is that we can produce 20 markets worth of of planning in a matter of hours because we have this tech.
We also developed Engage for you, which is our crowning jewel right now.
That's bringing at least some attention to our streaming side.
Engage for, for you.
We own it, as Chris was saying.
And it allows an advertiser, an agency to, before they spend the first penny in a campaign, they can see exactly how to to allocate money between linear streaming with tremendous intel behind it.
We have a license with Video Amp.
They're one of the stronger.
Do you know, Are you familiar with Video Amp?
Yes.
Okay, you know who they are.
We're partnered with them and it is a paid license.

But our tech, with our partners in the DSP world, what we have automated in house, we've automated pacing, which is the logging of all of the the activity week by week so we can see how it's performing.
If anything drops out, we put it back in.
Our performance ratio is like 99.9%.
What falls out that doesn't get put back in is usually technical difficulty in the last week.
So we have a lot of satisfaction from clients that are used to seeing linear buys come in at 80%.
Usually if we can get a client to come on board, they're with us for a long time.
Linux started with me.
They really actually launched our company.
We still place buys for Linux heating and cooling 46 years later.
Not as strong as it used to be, but, you know, we have clients that have been with us 10, 15 years.
It's unusual in our realm to have that kind of legacy with our clients.
So I think, you know, as I was reading.
Oh, sorry, go ahead, go ahead.
I wanted to just also address the transparent part in increasing margins.
The way we feel we can increase our margin is by new clients.
There is so much exposure now of holding companies and large companies making humongous margins by fraudulent impression delivery through bots, et cetera.
There's a lot of talk about that.
Our strongest DSP partner has eliminated that, eliminated it not because they were caught, but because they felt it was dishonest.
And we have jumped on that bandwagon.

And I believe that's why we were able to increase our business over 50% year over year because we're providing a minimum of 30% more in a campaign compared to the trade desk, for example, which everyone's using or mountain, which their margins like 65%.
So I think that's where we have the opportunity to really shine by being truly transparent.
Having competitive margins, not outrageous margins in the wild west that's going on right now.
So I don't know if that addresses those six questions.
I think what we would like to see going forward is a partnership that will grow the streaming part of our business because that's where we need to grow.
Great.
And when you say partnership, I think it'd be great to sort of understand a little bit more in terms of really what you're looking for in a partner.
Is it, Are you.
Because again, everyone looks at this a little differently.
You know, we're not a holding company.
We are, most of us, who we.

Would bring onto the board and as advisors would be other founders of other tech enabled marketing services businesses, media businesses, experience in the areas, you know, we curate advisory boards and boards to really work with and support the business and what they, what their important needs are.
But staying, in a sense, independent isn't for everybody.
Some people want to be part of something larger.
They want to be part of a larger holding company or a larger media organization where they may have, oh, we can, we're 25 people.
We're looking to grow with someone who.
Has 250 people and have offices.
And we really want to expand into Latin America.
I'm kind of making up a variety.
Of different random things that people might hear.
But are, you know, what, what is, what are you looking for in a partner?
You know, is it expertise?
Is it hands on?
Is it, you know, be left alone to, you know, work on a strategic plan and, and execute it?
And you know, I'm just sort of.
Curious a little bit in terms of what you've envisioned through this process, like where, you know.
Well, I think the big holding company idea is not attractive to us.
What we would like to have is a partner that brings the resources to expand our staff, especially sales.
Because if we are able to do that, the growth potential of CTV is pretty awesome.
I think that number, that's number one.
We'd like to internally grow the company.
Not by a holding company adding 200 people that we don't know.
Our culture at CTV, it's very family oriented, it's horizontally structured.
We give bonuses to the entire staff every quarter.
If we have the business to support it, we have very little churn.
And I like to say one of the reasons I love to go into the office is just to hear people laughing.
We have a good time at ctv.
People are passionate about what they do.
I would like to bring more passionate people to the table to grow the company and make it the success it can be.
I'd like to jump in here, too.
Our ideal situation is partnering with another company that already has a vast network of direct clients.
Direct a client.
It is becoming more appealing because it's less volatile than we currently work with primarily agencies.
So a company that is a mix of direct to client and possibly some agencies that is doing media that we're not doing.
So maybe they're doing search and creative or, you know, branding.
And then a natural fit is for them to be able to unlock additional budget and offer media, which we do so well.
That would be a really good fit.
So another company that has those relationships would essentially, you know, tenfold grow our sales and networking power to then unlock a lot more projects in media dollars.
Does that make sense?
And then, you know, also, there's plenty of ways we can use AI more internally and learn from things that, you know, this other company has done as well.
But unlocking a whole network of additional clients would be a big benefit.
Great.
That's super helpful.
That gives me a lot to think about.
Yeah.
And thank you for the introduction to Fairview Health.
That would be awesome.
A wonderful way to start.
Yeah.
I'll reach out to Chris and just.
Confirm if TV is part of the mix.
If it's more radio and out of.
Home, I'll let you know also.
And, I mean, we could talk about it still.
But, yeah, something for the back half of the year where they're starting to think through the planning there.
They're a great client, great company, great group of people, and sort of really making moves and certainly locally and how they're expanding their business.
We took that over from Fallon.
They had been with Fallon forever, and, you know, Fallon had this, like, media division, and they weren't necessarily doing a good job.
You know, it's sort of what I like about your business and what I.
Like about specialists in general is, you.
Know, you could be saying, yeah, we can do it all, but the idea.
That you're saying, like, we are the.
Best at what we do, that's why.
People work with us.
And that's always been a sort of focus of mine.
And at one point, I ran a small holding company of specialist agencies, and.
That was just so much fun.
When you can really work with, like, the best at this and the best.
At that, like, you have so much choice.
Why work with a company who's, like, good at everything when you can work.
With the company who's, like, best at that?
So there's a lot, you know, I'll say is, you know, congratulations, 46 years in business is absolutely remarkable.
That's just incredible.
And to see, yeah.
That you continue to do such great work with great clients and how you've innovated and met the moment and so it's exciting.
Do you have any other questions for me?
Otherwise I'll regroup with Andy and Ahmed and we'll, we'll talk a little bit about what, what.
I guess I should just mention one other thing which is typically speaking when I'm looking at a business, there's sort of two approaches.
One is this is a standalone business that's growing, you know, consistently revenue and.
Profit and could serve as sort of like a platform and that becomes like the core business.
And then we go and look for other businesses to acquire who may be able to help us continue to grow.
And we create a bigger business together.
And then there are other businesses who, they might not be that core but.
That sort of that initial platform, but they would be a business that would.
Be very additive, like you mentioned, like a performance marketing agency bringing together the work that you do.
So you know, sometimes it's chicken egg.
And obviously it's all opportunistic.
Meaning like you're considering these conversations now, you might not be in six months.
But I'm talking right now to a.
Handful of performance marketing agencies as well.
So, you know, it's impossible always to nail the timing on these things.
But it could be a fun opportunity.
If we were to be able to bring together a very sort of like.
Fast growing performance marketing agency who's doing.
Great work in search and social but not doing anything, especially in Dr. TV or linear.
And maybe this is an opportunity for.
Us to, to bring everyone together.
So yeah, I think you understand that vision, whether it's search or you know, search, social like you mentioned, and maybe even that creative part as well.
There's so many good creative agencies that have these relationships as well.
So all of those things work well together.
So yeah, I think, I think you get that vision.
Great.
Wonderful.
Well, Michael, thank you for all the kind words and giving us all this time.
I think you really nailed exactly what we are looking for.
So it's exciting.
We'll see if what we can do going forward.
And as you can see, Chris is ready to take over the business.
So you have a CEO in place.
It's pretty exciting all the way around.
Excellent.
I've been here for a long time though.
I had a feeling, I had a feeling.
Not 46 years, but you know.
Yeah, it's not 46, but it's been a long time.
I know.
I know the business and everybody quite well, and we are ready to explode and take on more.
So it's been a pleasure meeting you.
You, too.
Same.
Okay, well, thanks, everybody.
Yeah.
Michael.
We'll follow up with the date room access, if everybody's happy to move forward, and we'll go from there.
Great.
Right.
Thank you, everybody.
Thanks, everyone.
Have a good day.
Enjoy the rest of your day.
Cheers.
Cheers.

summary.overview:
- **Axle's Market Shift:** Axle exited three media businesses, aiming to reassess opportunities in CTV and connected TV.  
- **CTV Revenue Growth:** CTV grew revenue by 52% year over year, with strong growth plans through 2027.  
- **Leadership Evolution:** New CEO Chris Locke focuses on operational efficiency and leveraging proprietary technology for growth.  
- **Tech-Driven Advantages:** Their proprietary platforms ensure rapid planning, with a 99.9% performance ratio in campaign management.  
- **Client Loyalty:** Legacy clients like Linux Heating and Cooling demonstrate CTV’s strong, long-term client relationships, crucial for retention.  
- **New Opportunities:** Potential partnership with Fairview Health could enhance local media capabilities and expand service offerings.
summary.short_summary: The discussion centered on Axle's recent exit from three media businesses as part of a strategic shift to explore new growth areas in connected TV (CTV). CTV experienced a significant 52% revenue growth year over year, with plans for continued expansion. Leadership transitioned to Chris Locke as CEO, with a focus on operational efficiency and leveraging proprietary technology for competitive advantage. CTV's unique positioning combines traditional media and streaming, and their investment in proprietary technology ensures efficient campaign management with high performance ratios. The meeting also highlighted strong client loyalty, exemplified by legacy clients like Linux Heating and Cooling, and the potential partnership with Fairview Health for expanding service offerings.
